summary: Republican Sen. Darline Graham was appointed to this seat after Sen. Lindsey Graham died in July 2026, and she ran to keep it. Democrat Annie Andrews won, defeating her.

candidates.name: Annie Andrews
candidates.bio: Annie Andrews is a pediatrician and was the 2022 Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 1st congressional district. She won the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in the June 2026 primary.

positions.summary: Supports suspending the federal fuel tax for drivers and businesses, and opposes the on-and-off tariffs, which she calls unconstitutional.
Says she would stop the Medicaid cuts, restore the enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits and back a public option rather than Medicare for All.
Says her party has been weak on border security and that she supports deporting people who break immigration law.
Says she would fully fund public schools and special education, raise teacher and staff pay, and expand affordable child care and free or discounted school meals.
Says she favors an all-of-the-above approach to energy, including nuclear, and supports a two-year pause on new data center construction in South Carolina.
Pledges to restore Roe v. Wade protections and expand access to contraception, infertility care and rural maternal health.

candidates.name: Darline Graham
candidates.bio: Darline Graham was appointed to the U.S. Senate in July 2026 to serve the rest of the term of her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, after his death. She won the Republican nomination in an August runoff.

positions.summary: Says she would focus on cutting taxes and reducing federal spending, and her platform calls for making the Trump tax cuts permanent.
Lists rural hospitals and protecting Medicare among her priorities.
Supports completing the border wall, increasing enforcement and denying taxpayer-funded benefits to people in the country illegally.
Introduced a resolution for a Religious Education Week, and said faith-based schools are "a testament to the right of parents to choose an education that reflects their family's faith and values."
Says data centers "should have to pay for any new energy infrastructure they need," and cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act.
Says she is "proud to be pro-life" and cosponsored bills that would prohibit approval of new abortion drugs and permanently bar tax dollars from funding abortion.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35); also confirmed by wbtv.com report. Lindsey Graham's death (July 11) and Darline Graham's July appointment are reported by wbtv.com and thegreenpapers.com. Vote totals read Nov. 25 from thegreenpapers.com. Write-ins are in the total. abcnews4.com reported that the State Election Commission certified the results, but the certified count itself was not opened, so the race is not marked certified.
